source: the ice that is part of the ring sheet itself: sizes in planet radii, angles in degrees. Read by ice.ts. Wakes and grain lie on rows in radius; a row turns rigidly at the orbital rate of its radius, so every piece rides its own orbit and the rows shear against each other. Every piece is filtered by the size of the pixel and fades out where it gets smaller than a pixel. The blocks that can be seen one by one are in blocks.json.

orbit.note: the radius of the orbit that keeps pace with the globe's spin (the spin itself is spinDegPerSecond in plan.ts); the other orbits follow from it by Kepler's third law

note: tau: the share of a wake's tone that also moves the optical depth. glintWhite: how far a spark of the sand is white rather than the colour of the ice. weakest: the tone of the faintest wake over the tone of the strongest. filter and fade: the half width of the filter of a wake's edge in pixels, and the size in pixels under which a wake is gone and over which it is whole.

wakes.note: long soft patches of the sheet, darker or brighter, that ride the orbit: they show that the plane turns. Each class in two sets of rows, the second half a row out from the first. Per class: radial size of a cell; how many times longer the cell is along the orbit; the pitch of the patch's long axis to the orbit; the share of cells that hold a patch; the patch's radial half size in cells, smallest and largest; how soft its edge is (0 a hard disc, 1 a soft blob); how far a dark patch and a bright patch move the logarithm of the brightness. Wakes show only near the sheet (not in the hold).

spokes.note: soft radial smudges on the dense ring that turn with the globe. span: the radii they lie between; edge: how softly they end there; strength: how far the strongest moves the logarithm of the brightness (seen against the light they are bright); per spoke: its azimuth in the middle of the hold (degrees, against the turn of the orbits), its half width in degrees, how far it leans per radius, its tone over the strongest. Spokes show only near the sheet (not in the hold).

grain.note: the sand of the sheet. It has grains of many sizes, from finest by doublings; a size is a pair, across and along the orbit, and each size is a field of smooth noise that lies in the sheet, every row of cells on its own orbit. Seen at a slant a round grain would be a dash, so what a layer shows at a point is the sand whose grains are its number of pixels across and along the orbit there, blended between the sizes next to that; where the sheet is so far that the coarsest sand is finer than that, the sand merges into the sheet. Per layer: pixels; dense and thin: how far it moves the logarithm of the brightness in the dense and in the thin rings; sparks: 1 if its brightest grains are white sparks. hard: a grain's edge takes the share 1 minus twice this of the way to the next grain (0: the smoothest noise). tau: the share of the brightness that also moves the optical depth. far: the share of the sand's strength that is left in the hold (the sand is seen by the logarithm of the camera's height, as the light is). spark: how strong the sparks are in the dense and in the thin rings, each in the hold and in the skim (in units of the stones' gloss), from the first value of the noise to the second. spark.gain: the brightness of a spark. sweep: the share of the way the pixel's point slides over the ice during one take by which the grain and the ringlets are filtered (1: the true blur of the shutter).
